test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 13 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What does the Right to Constitutional Remedies mean ?

options.text: If any citizen feels the fundamental rights have been violated by the State, then they can move the court.
All linguistic and religious minorities can set up their own education institutions.
Any person has the right to move freely and live anywhere in India.
Each and every person is equal before the law, which means everyone will receive the same protection as per the laws of the country.

solution:
The correct answer is** __If any citizen feels the fundamental rights have been violated by the State, then they can move the court__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 32 is the Fundamental Rights and confers the right to constitutional remedies. 
 
• It contains provisions of the right to move the Supreme Court and the Supreme Court shall have the power to issue directions or orders or writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• High Courts are also entitled to enforce these provisions under Article 226.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**If rights are like guarantees, they are of no use if there is no one to honour them.

 
• The fundamental rights in the Constitution are important because they are enforceable.
 
• We have a right to seek the enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• This is called the Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• This itself is a Fundamental Right.
 
• This right makes other rights effective.
 
• It is possible that sometimes our rights may be violated by fellow citizens, private bodies or by the government.
 
• When any of our rights are violated we can seek a remedy through the courts.
 
• If it is a Fundamental Right we can directly approach the Supreme Court or the High Court of a state.
 
• That is why Dr Ambedkar called the Right to Constitutional Remedies, ‘the heart'.
